newsitem.title: CHINA: China sets July price for state-allocated metals.
newsitem.headline: China sets July price for state-allocated metals.

text.p: China Nonferrous Industry Trade Group, the government corporation responsible for allocating metals to key state enterprises, has set copper and aluminium prices for July, China Securities newspaper said on Wednesday.
Copper had been set at 20,854 yuan ($2,512) per tonne and aluminium at 13,483 yuan ($1,624) per tonne, the newspaper said. It did not give comparative figures.
Traders said the price had been set some weeks ago, before recent falls in both the futures price on the Shanghai Metal Exchange, and the local physical price.
The spot copper price was around 20,300 yuan in the Shanghai area and the aluminium physical price around 13,500 yuan, local traders said.

Shanghai copper futures opened sharply down on Wednesday, following falls overnight on the London Metal Exchange (LME), with the most actively traded November contract opening at 20,100 yuan per tonne, down 250 yuan from Tuesday's close.
Further falls were likely, both local and Western traders have said, as supply was seen higher than demand in a market severely lacking cash to buy either raw materials or finished products.
LME copper ended Tuesday down at $2,280, just above the day's lows, and London analysts said they saw the red metal probing downside support at $2,250 and $2,230 a tonne.
